# R1.13 -- Presenting complaints in single- vs multi-algorithm presentations

*Supplementary analysis for the IJPDS revision. Generated by `r1_11_r1_13_single_vs_multiple.R` from `ANALYSIS/ed_single.parquet` (N = 201,106). Presenting complaints are the twelve free-text chief-complaint clusters used in the main paper.*

## Verdict

Presenting complaints do differ between single- and multi-algorithm presentations, and they differ along the same severity gradient seen in the demographic comparison: 6 of the twelve complaint clusters exceed the |SMD| > 0.1 threshold. Presentations flagged by **more than one** algorithm are over-represented for musculoskeletal complaints (percentages given as MULTIPLE vs SINGLE): **Leg + knee pain** (13.4% vs 7.5%, SMD -0.192); **Lower back pain** (13.9% vs 10.3%, SMD -0.111).

Presentations flagged by **only one** algorithm are over-represented for a quite different set (percentages given as SINGLE vs MULTIPLE): **Chest pain + dyspnea** (9.1% vs 3.9%, SMD +0.214); **Alcohol intoxication** (3.7% vs 0.8%, SMD +0.195); **Nausea vomiting** (6.7% vs 3.1%, SMD +0.169); **Suicidal ideation** (2.0% vs 0.3%, SMD +0.162). Influenza-like illness and wound evaluation are also commoner among multi-algorithm presentations, and fall/transfer commoner among single-algorithm presentations, but these fall just below the threshold.

The pattern is clinically coherent. A diagnosis-based rule, a resource-based rule and a triage-based rule can all independently agree that a limb-pain, back-pain, minor-wound or influenza-like presentation is non-emergent, so these accumulate multiple flags. Chest pain and dyspnoea, alcohol intoxication, vomiting and suicidal ideation instead satisfy one criterion at a time -- a benign final diagnosis, or low resource use, or a low triage score -- but rarely all three, because they are triaged as urgent and investigated even when the eventual diagnosis is benign; they therefore accumulate single flags.

The relationship is graded rather than binary: moving from one to two to three concurring algorithms raises the share of Influenza like illness (7.5% -> 8.9% -> 18.2%), Leg + knee pain (7.5% -> 13.0% -> 16.8%) and Lower back pain (10.3% -> 13.5% -> 16.9%), and lowers the share of Chest pain + dyspnea (9.1% -> 4.3% -> 0.5%), Nausea vomiting (6.7% -> 3.4% -> 0.4%) and Abdomen pain (13.1% -> 13.0% -> 1.8%), with 11 of the twelve clusters moving monotonically.

**Why this analysis carries more weight than the acuity and admission comparisons.** Triage acuity and admission status are *inputs* to two of the three algorithms, so differences in them between single- and multi-algorithm presentations are largely forced by construction (see Part 2B of the R1.11 file). The free-text chief complaint is not used by any of the three algorithms -- the Diagnosis algorithm uses the primary discharge diagnosis, the Resources algorithm uses rhythm documentation, ED medication dispensing and disposition, and the Triage-Acuity algorithm uses the ESI score -- so the complaint-cluster contrast is not definitional. It is also empirically stable: removing the admission channel entirely by restricting to non-admitted presentations leaves every cluster SMD essentially unchanged (Part 3e). Together with ED length of stay, this is the evidence that actually supports a severity-gradient reading of algorithm agreement.

> **A note on inference.** Group sizes are 72,236 versus 28,332; every cluster difference is nominally significant at conventional thresholds, so p-values are not reported. Clusters are ranked by the standardised mean difference `(p1 - p2) / sqrt((p1(1-p1) + p2(1-p2))/2)`, with |SMD| > 0.1 flagged as non-negligible.

## Part 3e -- Sensitivity: are these differences definitional?

Chief complaint is not an input to any of the three algorithms, so unlike triage acuity and admission status (Part 2B of the R1.11 file) the complaint contrast is not forced by construction. As a check, the table below recomputes every cluster SMD after excluding admitted presentations, which removes the one channel through which the Resources algorithm's definition could propagate into the complaint mix.

| Cluster | Presenting-complaint cluster | SINGLE % (raw) | MULTIPLE % (raw) | SMD raw | SMD, non-admitted only | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | Chest pain + dyspnea | 9.1 | 3.9 | +0.214 | +0.198 | -0.016 |
| 8 | Alcohol intoxication | 3.7 | 0.8 | +0.195 | +0.222 | +0.026 |
| 6 | Leg + knee pain | 7.5 | 13.4 | -0.192 | -0.184 | +0.008 |
| 9 | Nausea vomiting | 6.7 | 3.1 | +0.169 | +0.163 | -0.006 |
| 10 | Suicidal ideation | 2.0 | 0.3 | +0.162 | +0.178 | +0.016 |
| 0 | Lower back pain | 10.3 | 13.9 | -0.111 | -0.094 | +0.017 |
| 11 | Fall transfer | 2.9 | 1.5 | +0.099 | +0.110 | +0.011 |
| 1 | Influenza like illness | 7.5 | 9.9 | -0.085 | -0.094 | -0.008 |
| 7 | Wound evaluation | 16.9 | 19.2 | -0.060 | -0.076 | -0.015 |
| 2 | Vehicle collision + Altered mental status | 12.9 | 14.3 | -0.041 | -0.019 | +0.023 |
| 5 | Abdomen pain | 13.1 | 11.8 | +0.040 | +0.032 | -0.008 |
| 4 | Shortness breath | 7.3 | 8.0 | -0.024 | -0.058 | -0.034 |

Every cluster SMD changes by less than 0.04 and none changes sign; the four largest effects (Chest pain + dyspnea, Alcohol intoxication, Leg + knee pain, Nausea vomiting) keep both their direction and their rank order. The set exceeding |SMD| > 0.1 shifts only at the margin: Lower back pain falls just below the threshold and Fall transfer rises just above it, leaving 6 clusters above it either way. The contrast with triage acuity, where the SMD falls from -0.792 to -0.264 once the definitional component is removed, and with admission, which cannot be compared cleanly at all, is stark. The complaint-cluster findings are therefore robust and can carry interpretive weight that the acuity and admission comparisons cannot.
